breaks.quote: Two lessons, 10 years apart. Most of us only ever learn the first one.
breaks.why: The second lesson is never stated plainly, so the reader has to guess what it is and how it applies to them.

breaks.quote: Because it is not finished with you. It still has a lesson to teach, and you have not learned it yet.
breaks.why: The surprising claim that regret exists to teach a lesson is given no example or reason beyond restating itself.

breaks.quote: And when you cannot answer, tell it as a story about somebody else and find the moral. That is why there is a chimpanzee in my notes.
breaks.why: The step from retelling a memory as another's story to finding its lesson is skipped, so the chimpanzee link is a leap.

breaks.quote: He tried out his opening line on his morning customers. Before December, he was confident.
breaks.why: The steps from trying one line on customers to confidence are missing, so the reader must guess how the change happened.
